statement.p: (b) Find the rate of change of f in the direction \nabla f_P.
(c) Find the rate of change of f in the direction of a vector making an angle of 45^\circ with \nabla f_P.

static.solution:
(a) We compute the gradient of f( x,y )=x{e}^{{x}^2-y}. The partial derivatives are  rac{\partial f}{\partial x}=1\cdot {e}^{{x}^2-y}+x{e}^{{x}^2-y}\cdot 2x={e}^{{x}^2-y}\left(1+2{x}^2ight)  rac{\partial f}{\partial y}=-x{e}^{{x}^2-y} The gradient vector is thus 
abla f = \left\lt  rac{\partial f}{\partial x}, rac{\partial f}{\partial y} ight> =\left\lt {e}^{{x}^2-y}\left(1+2{x}^2ight),-x{e}^{{x}^2-y} ight> ={e}^{{x}^2-y}\left\lt 1+2{x}^2,-x ight> At the point P=( 2,4 ) we have 
abla {f}_{P}={e}^0\left\lt 1+8,-2 ight> = \left\lt 9,-2 ight>\Downarrow\| 
abla {f}_{P}\| =\sqrt{{9}^2+{( -2 )}^2}=\sqrt{85} (b) The rate of change of f in the direction of the gradient vector is the length of the gradient, that is,
\| 
abla {f}_{P}\| =\sqrt{85}.
(c) Let {\mathbf{e}}_{\mathbf{v}} be the unit vector making an angle of {45}^{\circ } with 
abla {f}_{P}.
The rate of change of f in the direction of {\mathbf{e}}_{\mathbf{v}} is the directional derivative of f in the direction {\mathbf{e}}_{\mathbf{v}},
which is the following dot product: {D}_{\mathbf{{e}_{v}}} f(P) =
abla {f}_{P}\cdot \mathbf{{e}_{v}}=\| 
abla {f}_{P}\| \| \mathbf{{e}_{v}}\| \cos {45}^{\circ }=\sqrt{85}\cdot 1\cdot  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{42.5}\approx 6.5192
